sentences.text: The application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short, 'BNSS') for an order of pre-arrest bail.

2. The petitioners are the accused 1 to 3 in Crime No.714/2024 of the Vadanappally Police Station,
Thrissur, which is registered against them for allegedly committing the offence punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (in short, 'IPC').
3.
The prosecution case, in brief, is that: the 1 st accused was married to the defacto complainant on 16.06.2021.
The accused 2 and 3 are the parents of the 1 st accused.

During the period of cohabitation of the defacto complainant in the matrimonial house with the accused persons, they mentally and physically harassed the defacto BAIL APPL. NO. 8119 OF 2024 2024:KER:83504 complainant demanding more dowry.
They also misappropriated her property.
Thus, the accused have committed the above offences.

4. Heard; Sri.Satheesh N., the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, and Sri.C.S.Hrithwik,
the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are innocent of the accusations leveled against them.
There is no material to substantiate the petitioners' culpability in the crime.

The fact that the 1 st petitioner was married to the defacto complainant on 16.06.2021,
but Annexure A1 FIR is registered only on 11.09.2024, proves the falsity and frivolity in the crime.
There is no plausible explanation for the delay.
The marital relationship between the 1st petitioner and the defacto complainant is strained.
It is only to pressurize the petitioners to yield to the defacto complainant's unlawful demand, she has registered the present FIR.
The petitioners are law abiding citizen without any criminal antecedents.
BAIL APPL.
The petitioners are willing to abide by any stringent condition that may be imposed by this Court.

Hence,

2 the application may be allowed.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
He submitted that the investigation is only at the preliminary stage.
He also submitted that if the petitioners are granted orders of pre-arrest bail, it may hamper the investigation.
Hence, the application may be dismissed.
7. The prosecution allegation is that, the petitioners, had mentally and psychically harassed the defacto complainant demanding more dowry.
The materials on record reveal that the 1st petitioner was married to the defacto complainant on 16.06.2021.
However, Annexure-A1 FIR has registered only on 11.09.2024.
Prima facie, there is no plausible explanation for the delay.
It is also apparent the marital relationship is strained.
However, these are matters to be investigated and ultimately decided after trial.

8. In Bhadres Bipinbhai Sheth vs State of Gujarat and another [2015 KHC 4579], the Hon'ble BAIL APPL. NO. 8119 OF 2024 2024:KER:83504 Supreme Court has succinctly culled out the principles for the purpose of grant of an order of pre-arrest bail in offences of a similar nature, by holding that the complaint made against the accused has to be thoroughly examined at the stage of considering a bail application, especially to find out if it is a false or frivolous complaint.

entities.text: Bhadres Bipinbhai Sheth vs State of Gujarat and another [2015 KHC 4579]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The courts should examine whether there is any family dispute between the parties and whether the Investigating Officer is acting in connivance with the complainant.
The gravity of each charge and the exact role of the accused should also be properly comprehended.

The discretion to grant an order of prearrest bail must be exercised on the basis of the available materials and the facts of the particullar case and there is no requirement that the accused must make out a special case to exercise the power of grant of anticipatory bail.

The discretion of the Court should be exercised with due care and circumspection, and the frivolity in the prosecution should be examined, particularly whether any harassment, humiliation or unjustified detention of the accused.

After bestowing my anxious consideration to the facts, the materials placed on record, and the rival submissions made across the Bar, and taking note of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the afore-cited decision, and on considering the fact that the marital relationship between the 1st petitioner and the defacto complainant is strained and there are disputes pending between them, and further that there is a delay in registering the FIR, I am satisfied and convinced that the petitioners had made out valid grounds to invoke the discretionary jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the BNS.
Hence, I am inclined to allow the application, but subject to stringent conditions.

In the result, the application is allowed subject to the following conditions:
(i) The petitioners are directed to surrender before the Investigating Officer within one week from today;
